To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PK/PD model of MPL action in rat liver is capable of describing both dose dependent and tolerance effects for GR mRNA/GR and TAT mRNA/T AT induction.
The dose dependence and tolerance for TAT mRNA and enzyme induction were observed in adrenalectomised rats treated with methylprednisolones (MPL) at different dosing regimens.

(1) the GR density in rat liver is down regulated by MPL in a dose dependent manner, and (2) the induction of TAT mRNA and enzyme activity is mediated by the GR density in a dose dependent and tolerant manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dose dependence and repeated dose effects on GR down regulation and TAT induction in rat liver.
the development of a PK/PD model for receptor/gene mediated pharmacodynamics of steroid drugs.
developing a PK/PD model to predict the pharmacodynamics of MPL on GR down regulation and TAT induction in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GR down regulation and TAT mRNA/Tat induction by MPL in rat liver are dose dependent, and tolerance develops to the latter after a single dose of MPL.
the GR mRNA/GR and the TAT mRNA/Tat induction models are the most appropriate models for the MPL PK/PD data in rat liver.
the dose dependence and repeated dose effects on GR density and TAT induction are consistent with our fourth generation model and challenge our previous model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GR down regulation and TAT induction are dose dependent, but not time dependent.
a PK/PD model for the GR mRNA/GR density down regulation and TAT mRNA/T AT induction in rat liver by MPL has been developed and tested for dose dependence and tolerance.
the PK/PD approach has been successful in the design and evaluation of receptor/gene mediated pharmacodynamics for the GR and TAT systems in rat liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown the importance of using a pharmacokinetic/pharmocodynamic approach in order to better understand how a drug is working at the receptor/gene level and to develop better models for drug design.
we can develop a pharmacokinetic/pharmocodynamic (PK/PDT) model to predict the dose dependence and repeated dose effects in a rat model of methylprednisone (MPL).

the dose dependent and repeated dose responses of TAT induction can be explained by a model which incorporates the dose dependence of the GR occupancy and tolerance effects on the receptor/gene mediated signal transduction.
